conflicts.title: Three fixes of accepted lists and five selected options add D1 writes
conflicts.what: The standing rule says that the number of D1 writes must not increase. D1 counts each INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE as rows written, and each index adds one written row when a write includes the indexed column. Example: an INSERT into a table with 2 indexes counts as 3 written rows. Eight places add writes. (1) D-DATA-01: 6 new indexes or more (D1-07, D1-08): one more written row for each insert into operations_events, visonaut_status_outbox, visonaut_checks, visonaut_runs, operations_check_creations, and visonaut_promotions (2 of the 6 are partial indexes, which add the row only while the row matches their condition). (2) D-DATA-01: the table pull_request_titles (D1-03): one written row for each pull_request webhook in the form of the sketch, and one row only for a new pull request or a new title when the statement skips an equal title. (3) D-OPS-01 row 8: a heartbeat row at the end of each pass: the cron runs each 5 minutes, so 288 writes each day. The cursor statements of a pass skip an equal value, so an unchanged cursor writes no row today; nobody counted all written rows of one idle pass. (4) D-DATA-04: the 30-day window deletes retention pins and then image rows that stay for ever today; a DELETE is a write. (5) D-AUTH-05: one UPDATE one time, one row for each GitHub account (10 organization members at most). (6) D-AUTH-03: a new review session row in the rare case of an expired review session. (7) D-OPS-05: each reserve call that the capacity check refuses writes 3 rows (the capacity snapshot, and two writes of the alert row), and the wait of the selected option sends that call again. The CLI of today sends it one time. Example: a wait of 20 minutes with one try each 30 seconds is 40 tries and 120 written rows for one job. (8) D-WORK-06: a whole-screenshot decision by mistake is saved and then reversed, which is 2 saved commands where the dialog of today saves none (the button path only, and only for a mistake). Three places add no row: the new column of D-RUN-02, the closed reason of D-UX-04, and the settings count of D-AUTH-04, if each one is a column in a write that exists.
evidence: Cloudflare D1 pricing, read 2026-10-06 (page updated Apr 21, 2026), https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/platform/pricing/ : 'Write operations include INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE'; 'Indexes will add an additional written row when writes include the indexed column, as there are two rows written'; Workers Paid: 50 million rows written each month included, then 1.00 USD for each million; rows read: 25 billion included, then 0.001 USD for each million.

conflicts.title: Five answers repair the queued save path, and the server has a direct path that needs none of them
conflicts.what: The page always sends a decision with queued: true. The server stores a task row, answers HTTP 202, and the page polls for the receipt. Example: the reviewer presses A on one variant. The page sends POST /api/comparisons/<id>/commands and gets 202 with a command ID. A later pass of the server saves the decision. The page asks GET /api/commands/<command ID>/queued until the answer is the receipt. On the direct path the same POST saves the decision and answers 200 with the result. The reason for the queue is contract line 196: processing continues after the window closes. D-RES-02 (no-promise) stops telling the reviewer that the window can close. Then four fixes still serve the queue: the receipt with no model (D-RUN-05), the poll with shorter waits (D-RUN-01, REVIEW-07), one poll loop and a 'still queued' text after 30 s (D-RES-01 row 6), and a queued decision whose write fails 5 times (D-OPS-01 row 12). D-RES-05 (open) exists because the queued answer has no reviewer field. The server also has a direct path with no product caller: it saves in the request and returns the result with no model when the revisions agree, and its conflict answer names the reviewer of the row that conflicted. One queued decision writes 13 rows or more for its task row alone, and the row is deleted later, which is one more write. This cost exists today: no selected answer adds to it.

On a conflict the direct branch answers through conflictResponse (review.ts:682-697), which adds the 'reviewer' of the row that conflicted: that is the field that D-RES-05 misses in the queued answer. D-LOAD-04.question: This sounds more like an idiomatic solution, right? The inline script seems hacky.
D-LOAD-04.shortAnswer: Yes. The maintainer is right. A route loader that returns a promise, with a streamed document, is the way that the TanStack Start documentation describes. The head request is a script that this repository would write by hand, and no page of the documentation describes it. The audit recommended it for its lower risk, not because it is the usual way. One limit: the loader also puts an inline script in the document, but the router writes it, not this repository. One part is not from the documentation: the API of this app is its own request handler (handleApi), outside the framework, so the loader on the server needs a small bridge to the access check of that handler.

documentation.fact: A route loader runs on the server for the first document and in the browser for a navigation.
documentation.quote: Route loaders are isomorphic - they run on both server and client, not just the server.

documentation.fact: A server function is code that only the server runs. A loader can call it.
documentation.quote: Server functions let you define server-only logic that can be called from anywhere in your application - loaders, components, hooks, or other server functions. […] On the client, calls become fetch requests to the server.

documentation.fact: A loader can return a promise that it does not await. The server then sends the page shell first and the data after it.
documentation.quote: To defer slow or non-critical data, return an unawaited/unresolved promise anywhere in your loader response […] Streaming requires a server that supports it and for TanStack Router to be configured to use it properly. […] As deferred promises resolve, their results (or errors) are serialized and streamed to the client via an inline script tag

documentation.fact: A route can run its loader on the server and draw its component only in the browser.
documentation.quote: Run loader on the server and send the loader data to the client. Disable server-side rendering of the route component. […] For the first route with ssr: false or ssr: 'data-only', the server will render the route's pendingComponent as a fallback. […] At runtime, a child route inherits the Selective SSR configuration of its parent. However, the inherited value can only be changed to be more restrictive (i.e. true to data-only or false and data-only to false).

documentation.fact: One function can have a server form and a browser form.
documentation.quote: Compose a single function that adapts to both client and server environments.

needs.why: Then the document sends its shell at once and the list streams after it. With await, the first byte waits for D1: 0.9 to 2.0 s today where the document takes 41 to 119 ms. After the fixes of D-LOAD-01 and D-LOAD-03 the wait is about 0.3 s (estimate: 3 D1 round trips of about 105 ms each), and more when the GitHub permission is not stored.

needs.need: Keep one endpoint and one access check: on the server the loader calls the handler of /api/runs in the same process, with the cookies of the document request. In the browser it fetches /api/runs as today.
needs.why: This is the 'separately scoped authenticated server read' that the note of P03 names, in its smallest form. The access check of D-LOAD-03 (2 round trips), the rule of 60 seconds for the GitHub permission, the 401, 403, and 503 answers, and the origin check stay one piece of code (apps/web/src/api/index.ts:110, :194-207). The way that the documentation names first is a server function. In this app it would be a second private endpoint: the browser would call it at a path of the framework, and apps/web/src/server.ts sends each path that is not /api/, /v1/, or /images/ to the page renderer, so the checks of handleApi would not run for it. needs.need: Do not renew the session cookie in this read.

If the document request makes it, the database row is renewed and the cookie in the browser is not, and the next API request then finds a session that is not due for a renewal (reasoning from the updateAge rule; nobody tested it). So the server read must turn the renewal off: the installed Better Auth 1.7.5 has the option disableRefresh, and requireMaintainer has no parameter for it today (packages/security/src/authorization.ts:32-36 passes disableCookieCache only). That is one new parameter in the shared check.

D-CODE-05.question: This looks like the idiomatic way to work with wrangler?
D-CODE-05.shortAnswer: Yes for the database and the storage. Local D1 and local R2 that keep their state in .wrangler/state, with migrations and seed data from wrangler commands with --local, is the documented way. Two parts of this option are not a Wrangler feature and need code of the repository: a signed local session, and answers for the GitHub requests.

documentation.fact: The dev server makes local copies of D1 and R2 and keeps them in one folder. The Vite plugin and Wrangler share it.
documentation.quote: Miniflare automatically creates local versions of your resources (like KV, D1, or R2). […] By default, both Wrangler and the Vite plugin store local binding data in the same location: the .wrangler/state folder in your project directory.
documentation.source: Cloudflare Workers, Local data (page updated Jun 25, 2026), https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/development-testing/local-data/

documentation.fact: Seed data goes in with wrangler commands and the flag --local.
documentation.quote: npx wrangler d1 execute <DATABASE_NAME> --command="<SQL_QUERY>" --local  |  npx wrangler r2 object put <BUCKET>/<KEY> --file=<PATH_TO_FILE> --local

documentation.fact: Migrations run on the local database with --local. A local session cannot reach production data.
documentation.quote: wrangler d1 migrations apply your-database --local […] Without the --local flag, the commands are executed against the remote version of your D1 database […] A local session does not have access to your production data by default.

documentation.fact: The Vite plugin keeps state in the same folder by default.
documentation.quote: persistState: An optional override for state persistence. By default, state is persisted to .wrangler/state.

documentation.fact: With the Vite plugin, an environment variable selects the Wrangler environment. Secrets for local use come from a file for that environment.
documentation.quote: you select a Cloudflare environment at dev or build time by providing the CLOUDFLARE_ENV environment variable. […] Running vite dev or vite build without providing CLOUDFLARE_ENV will use the default top-level Cloudflare environment. […] If .dev.vars.<environment-name> exists then only this will be loaded; the .dev.vars file will not be loaded.
